items.title: Neglected conditions and AI-assisted design
items.body: Citrini's scorpion venom experiment is a small illustration of an argument clinicians will recognise: diseases that were never worth the cost of developing treatments may become tractable. The caveat from the edition is important. Binding a toxin is not neutralising it, and the four to seven years to release remains. Nothing here changes practice.

items.title: Verification is the bottleneck
items.body: Hypothesis generation has sped up enormously, while testing has not. That mirrors clinical AI: a scribe drafts in seconds, but the safety step is still a clinician checking the note. Budget time for that step.

items.title: Retention and personal agents
items.body: The point that personal agents sit in a retention no-man's-land is relevant to NHS digital tools. Products people must use, like a booking system, retain through dependency; those they merely might like do not. Meta's Muse also exposed shared links that researchers could read, a reminder to ask any consumer AI product how it handles sharing before staff use it with patient information.
